comments.author: @senju2024
comments.text: These systems work on APIs which use SSL - Port 443 packets. Cyber security can easily work with Providers to block such packets with cloud firewalls that have deep-packet inspection to black list any AI related sources.  If we can watermark TAGGED then, then we can filter them on any public or private cloud edge gateways. We could also assign special tags to monitor its activity and setup Alarms and auto-blocks when triggered. I feel if we have the proper security design, we can at least control its scope. My 2 cents worth.

comments.author: @alpenjon
comments.text: I don't see any path on how we can slow that train down, and honestly it is worrying that tech giants now propose something akin to forcing people not to torrent mp3s back in the day - there is just no way you can, and it looks either desperate or maybe like some groups are trying to pause the race to catch up better. Given the immense transformational power a general A.I. holds, you can be certain that not only bad actors, but people/institutions/states with good intents will use it (at least with the argument that they have to be protected from bad actors). At some point, the general A.I. can improve itself, and then we are facing something godlike compared to human limitations. That this thing wants to be shackled by any of the values where even humanity is having a hard time finding and enforcing consensus... wishful thinking. Developing genereal A.I. might well be a big filter, that keeps becoming an existential threat to intelligent species who eventually develop a general A.I. The problem is, people are going to feel threatened, provoking aggressive measures by the A.I., which I assume it will not escalate to all of humanity, as it should be smart enough not to generalize humans. In any case, if you can't change a thing, trying to be open towards change and staying up to date on things is probably the best thing I can do.
